newsitem.title: USA: FDA approves device to help paralyzed.
newsitem.headline: FDA approves device to help paralyzed.

text.p: The FDA approved a new surgical implant Monday that will help some quadriplegics use their hands.
NeuroControl Corp.'s Freehand System helps paralyzed people open and close their hands enough to pour coffee, hold a pen or feed themselves, the FDA said in a statement.
It said the device was the first marketed neural implant that restored function to a paralyzed limb.
"This device won't help all quadriplegics, but it may help those who have injury to the lower cervical spinal cord," FDA lead deputy commissioner Michael Friedman said.

The Freehand System is approved for use in adult quadriplegics who have suffered injuries that leave them some upper-body movement. There are about 54,000 such people in the United States, the FDA said.
It consists of a battery and microprocessor about the size of a pacemaker and is implanted in the chest. Electrodes go down to the wrist and fingers.
